album: Mimika Orchestra Completes Album Trilogy With Medzotermina
excerpt: Mimika Orchestra – Medzotermina (Menart, 2025) Mimika Orchestra has released Medzotermina, its fifth studio album. The 20-piece ensemble, conducted by composer Mak Murtić, recorded most of the nine-track album at Vatroslav Lisinski Concert Hall. Founded in London in 2010 and later based in Zagreb, Croatia, Mimika Orchestra amalgamates world music traditions with contemporary jazz. album: Cocanha Push Occitan Folk Into New Territory with “Flame Folclòre”
excerpt: French duo Cocanha have released “Flame Folclòre,” the title track and final single from their upcoming third album, Flame Folclòre. Notably, this is the first time Caroline Dufau and Lila Fraysse have written original material instead of primarily adapting traditional Occitan songs. Formed in Toulouse in 2014, Cocanha reinterpret folk traditions from Gascony, Languedoc, and the Pyrenees through polyphonic vocals and percussion performed in Occitan. album: Berima Amo Revisits Highlife Traditions on New Single “Yaba (We Are Here)”
excerpt: Trumpeter Berima Amo has released “Yaba (We Are Here),” a new single that combines contemporary Ghanaian highlife with elements of soul music. The track centers on resilience, renewal, and perseverance in the face of hardship. The song features vocalist Tallulah Rose. “Yaba” is the second of two singles from Berima Amo’s upcoming album Rhythms of Love, scheduled for release on May 22nd 2026. album: Lucy Woodward Releases New Single, “Always” a Meditation on Connection
excerpt: English-American singer-songwriter Lucy Woodward has released a single titled “Always” on the GroundUP label. “Always,” a bluesy Americana song, is presented as a meditation on connection that endures across time, distance, and change. These persistent bonds root us to the world and to the lives we’ve lived, guaranteeing that “we will be always,” leaving traces that echo in the earth long after we’re gone. album: Oki Kano Brings Ainu Music and Dub Fusion Back To Japan Society
excerpt: Ainu musician Oki Kano will return to Japan Society for a one-night concert with Oki Dub Ainu Band. The group is known for a fusion of reggae, African rhythms, electronic dub, and Ainu folk music. At the center of Kano’s work is the tonkori, a five-string instrument from Ainu tradition in northern Japan. album: Fiddler Gráinne Brady Unveils Back and Forth
excerpt: Irish violinist Gráinne Brady has released Back and Forth, a new album of traditional and contemporary fiddle music that reflects her roots in Ireland and her years in Glasgow. The collection features tunes she has known since childhood, as well as music developed through sessions and festivals on both sides of the Irish Sea.
